headline: US chip and electronics prices jump 12.9%, fastest since 2004
text:
# US chip and electronics prices jump 12.9%, fastest since 2004

Factory-gate electronics prices in the US are running twenty times their usual pace, while Europe's energy numbers split: bills up, coal gone, renewables up.

## Today in the data

### US electronics prices break out
[US factory-gate prices: computers and electronics break out](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Computer and electronic producer prices rose 12.9% in the year to Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors), against a usual +0.63%. On the chart the line has never left the −2 to +2 band before 2026; electrical equipment (+4.4%) and machinery (+3.9%) are firm but ordinary. Worth checking against semiconductor supply in us-chips; the index is not seasonally adjusted and its base year differs from the others, so read growth only.

### Austrian household bills jump a third
[Household electricity, EUR per kWh, all taxes included](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austria paid €0.3272 per kWh in H2 2025, up 34.3% on a year earlier, the biggest rise since the series starts in 2008 (energy-household-eu); Luxembourg is up 31.7% to €0.2665. Look at the 2024 dip in the Austrian line: the jump is partly measured from a subsidised low base. Prices include all taxes and levies, so the move mixes wholesale power with the withdrawal of relief measures.

### Austrian pharma output halves
[Austrian pharma output falls back to earth (2021 = 100)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austrian pharma production (C21) was 160.4 in Jul 2026, down 45.7% on the year, the sharpest fall since 2011 (eu-ipi-sectors). The chart shows the comparison is with a spike near 295 in mid-2025, not a collapse to a normal level: at 160 output is still well above Germany's 97.9 and above Austria's whole-manufacturing index of 102.6. Monthly sector indices for small countries are volatile and revised.

### Britain's coal power is effectively over
[UK electricity generation by source, TWh](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
UK coal generation was 0.33 TWh in 2025, down 82.6% on 2024 and the sharpest fall in a record starting in 1921 (electricity-mix). Wind at 85.8 TWh now runs close to gas at 90.9 TWh — the crossover is the thing to watch on this chart. The last year is often Ember's provisional figure, so 2025 may be revised.

### Estonia's car market halves
[New car registrations in Estonia, by fuel](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Estonia registered 13,141 new cars in 2025, down 49% on 2024, with diesel down 70.4% to 1,738 (eu-car-registrations). Battery-electric cars, at 872, fell with the rest, so this reads as a demand shock rather than a switch of fuel — worth checking against Estonia's new car registration tax. Thirteen years of data only, and registrations can shift across a tax deadline.

### Greece past 60% renewable power
[Greece: renewables in electricity, % (Eurostat nrg_ind_ren)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Greece's renewable share of electricity reached 60.9% in 2025, up 9.65 points in a year against a usual 2.17 (eu-renewables-share). The chart's slope steepens sharply after 2022. This is the Renewable Energy Directive's accounting, not Ember's generation share, so it will not match the electricity-mix numbers used above.

### Egypt's FDI drops back to trend
[Egypt: net FDI inflows, current US dollars](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Egypt took $15.5bn of net FDI in 2025, $31.1bn less than in 2024 (macro-external), the largest fall since 1971. The chart shows 2024 as a lone spike, so this is a return towards the 2010s range rather than a slump below it. World Bank external data lag one to two years and are revised.

## Forecasts

### US electronics prices keep climbing
[us-ppi-sectors:computer_electronic: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The index stood at 120.048 in Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors). The tool chose Holt-Winters additive with a 12-month period and fits the past closely (MAPE 0.28%, residual sd 0.42). It projects 122.33 by Nov 2026, with a 95% band of 120.90 to 123.77 — the range in which the outcome should fall if the recent trend and noise carry on unchanged. A tariff change or an easing of semiconductor supply would put November outside it; so would the trend simply flattening, since the method extrapolates +0.98 points a month.

### Austrian pharma output rebuilds slowly
[eu-ipi-sectors:AT|C21: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 160.4 in Jul 2026 (eu-ipi-sectors). Holt-Winters additive was chosen again, but the fit is loose here (MAPE 5.1%, residual sd 11.8). The October point forecast is 167.1 with a 95% band of 127.0 to 207.2 — wide because this series lurches, and the band only describes past noise. A repeat of the 2025 production spike, or a plant outage, would fall outside it; Eurostat revisions to recent months are routine.

### Austrian bills tick down then back up
[energy-household-eu:AT: Holt-Winters forecast, 2 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austria's household price was €0.3272/kWh in H2 2025 (energy-household-eu). The method is Holt-Winters additive, period 2, with MAPE 3.3%. It gives €0.3249 for H2 2026, band €0.2904 to €0.3594, meaning the usual half-yearly wobble around the path. This is a heavily taxed, partly administered price: the projection extends its own past, not policy. A new levy, a relief scheme or a wholesale swing would take it outside the band.

## Correlations
- **Austria vs Luxembourg household electricity** (yoy, 2008-S2 to 2025-S2, n=35): r = 0.53 at lag 0 and 0.61 at lag −1, both clear the 0.359 band. Shared wholesale and tax-relief timing rather than one country leading the other; the lag-4 peak (0.64) is likely a fluke of nine tests.
- **US computer/electronic vs electrical equipment PPI** (yoy, 2011-01 to 2026-08, n=188): r = 0.58 with electrical leading by 4–5 months, clears the widened 0.504 band. Common input costs move both, but the 2026 electronics spike is far larger than electrical prices imply.

## What to watch
- us-ppi-sectors (last 2026-08): September PPI settles whether the 12.9% electronics jump is a level shift or a spike.
- eu-ipi-sectors (last 2026-07): August will show whether Austrian C21 stays near 160 or slides further.
- eu-car-registrations (last 2025): the 2026 annual file tests whether Estonia's collapse was a tax-timing effect.
- cpi-eu and eu-hicp (last 2026-07): August inflation shows how much of the electricity rise reached households.
- electricity-mix (last 2025): Ember's revision may lift UK coal off 0.33 TWh.

## Sources
- us-ppi-sectors — BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly; last 2026-08.
- eu-ipi-sectors — Eurostat sts_inpr_m industrial production, 2021=100, monthly; last 2026-07.
- energy-household-eu — Eurostat nrg_pc_204, band DC, all taxes included; last 2025-S2.
- electricity-mix — Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute, via Our World in Data; last 2025.
- eu-car-registrations — Eurostat road_eqr_carpda; last 2025.
- eu-renewables-share — Eurostat nrg_ind_ren; last 2025.
- macro-external — World Bank World Development Indicators; last 2025.
